display.purpose: The champions hero and the stacked masthead title on every other route.

title.purpose: Card names, group heads and timeline event headings.

body.purpose: Reading copy, tables and UI text; tabular numerals for stats. Repeated sizes are role tokens --type-card-title/data/meta/control/label.

label.purpose: Nav, chips, captions, table heads, flags and metadata; 11px minimum.

shadows.name: card-lift

shadows.name: press

shadows.name: selector-rest
shadows.purpose: The roster card's resting soft depth; emphasis comes from the red field and ink border.

shadows.name: selector-hover
shadows.purpose: Roster card shadow on hover or focus as the card lifts and its border turns brass.

motion.name: hero-breath
motion.purpose: Slow scale and drift of the champions photograph; paused offscreen.

motion.name: rule-pulse
motion.purpose: The brass identity rule beneath the hero identity line.

motion.name: strip-slide
motion.purpose: Facts rail loop; pauses offscreen, on hover and on keyboard focus.

motion.name: pointer-depth
motion.purpose: Home photo, copy and hangtag respond to pointer position.

motion.name: selector-duet
motion.purpose: The card lifts while the portrait rises 16px straight up and scales 1.05 from its feet, with no rotation.

motion.name: halftone-blobs
motion.value: 4 drifting blobs (2 on narrow screens), smooth radial falloff, 7-16s life
motion.purpose: A fine halftone where most dots stay at base size while a few soft blobs swell dots locally with a gradient edge; one batched fill per frame.

motion.name: result-reveal
motion.purpose: Result rows reveal once on scroll, then lift 6px on hover with a growing brass bar.

narrative.overview:
This is a fan-built team hub dressed as a seasonal streetwear lookbook. The team's red is not an accent on a neutral page: it is a garment-dyed ground that owns whole regions, with ink black, warm paper and one brass tone supporting it. The roster reads as a lineup, player details live on hangtags, and sections are joined by stitched rules rather than generic dividers. The result should feel like opening a collection, not scrolling a sports template.

The roster home (index.html) is the reference implementation. Its champions hero, facts rail, halftone field, off-grid selector rack, record table, history split and shop teaser are the most resolved expressions of this world. The other six routes — shop, matches, titles, media, community and the 404 — share the shell, tokens, reusable kit and baseline grid, each with a photographic masthead and a page-specific signature. When a decision is ambiguous, copy the home page before inventing a new treatment.

The site is deliberately unofficial. Every page states that it is fan-made, photography is credited as editorial reference, and the shop keeps official and fan-made merchandise apart behind a stitched line. Imagery is real team photography and transparent player cutouts from the club's own portrait set; no likeness is fabricated. Hierarchy comes from the contrast between a compressed display face and a workhorse grotesk, not from decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Red as ground, not trim; cream paper as the quiet counter-surface.
Hangtags, woven labels and stitched dividers as the component vocabulary.
Square corners throughout; no rounded UI chrome.
Three quiet loops: the champions photograph breathes, the facts rail slides, and soft blobs swell a fine halftone field; all pause offscreen and reduce away.
Honest, plainspoken copy that never implies team endorsement.
Tab stops are actions: the selector rack reveals one player at a time, and focus is never visually removed.
The primary navigation has four top-level entries, with the remaining pages grouped under "More" on small screens.

rules.name: The Home-First Rule
rules.body: The roster home is the reference surface. Copy what index.html does before inventing a new treatment, and treat the other pages as inheritors.

rules.name: The Real Action Rule
rules.body: Nothing is focusable without an action. The selector cards are buttons that reveal one player's detail; :focus-visible always keeps a brass outline, including under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Red Ground Rule
rules.body: If a region is red, its text is opaque cream. Tinted cream, muted gray and brass-on-red all fail; the red owns the region and the copy sits on top at full strength.

rules.name: The Single-Theme Rule
rules.body: The palette is exactly ten hex values, each equal to a declared token, with no dark-mode variant. A pinned single-theme brief is intentional: a scheme swap would replace the lookbook's material identity. Do not introduce one.

rules.name: The Role-Token Rule
rules.body: Repeated sizes are declared once in site.css and referenced everywhere: --type-display, --type-headline, --type-title, --type-card-title (22px), --type-body (16px), --type-data (14px), --type-meta (13px), --type-control (12px) and --type-label (11px), plus --type-index and the plate sizes. Genuine one-offs stay inline.

rules.name: The Eleven-Pixel Floor
rules.body: Nothing functional renders below 11px. The micro-label look comes from tracking and case, not from shrinking type.

rules.name: The True Weight Rule
rules.body: Anton has one real weight. Never let the UA default 700 or font-synthesis invent a bold cut; reset every Anton-bearing heading to 400. Prose stays within 45–75ch and card titles share one 22px role.

rules.name: The One Reading Path Rule
rules.body: Content text is always left-aligned. Only the punch-hole label on a hangtag and the small flag on a selector card are centred, because they are printed marks on an object rather than page copy. Each section has one heading, one line of purpose and one primary action.

rules.name: The Edge-First Rule
rules.body: Reach for a border before a shadow. A row of identical hairline-border-plus-wide-shadow cards is the default this world refuses.

rules.name: The Restrained Depth Rule
rules.body: No hard offset shadows. Depth comes from a 2–3px offset and a soft blur; emphasis comes from a brass border and the warm red field, not a giant coloured block behind the card.

rules.name: The Halftone Rule
rules.body: The dots are printed texture on cream paper, not a backdrop effect: they stay inside the section, keep one red at fixed opacity, and most stay at base size. Movement belongs to a few drifting blobs with a soft edge — never a uniform per-dot wave or a scaled, sliding field.

rules.name: The Tap-Target Floor
rules.body: Every inline text link shares one min-height: var(--tap) rule (28px), raised to 44px on coarse pointers along with chips and product links, plus :active feedback. Component padding stays local; the hit-area floor is global.

dos: Do let red occupy entire regions; never sprinkle it as a highlight on a white template.
Do use real team photography once per editorial moment and credit it as editorial reference on an unofficial page.
Do keep official and fan-made merchandise visibly separate with working outbound links.
Do state "unofficial fan hub" in the header and footer of every page.
Do judge new work against the roster home first, then check the other-page patterns above.
Do keep every tabbable element actionable and every focus state visible, especially under reduced motion.
donts: Don't add rounded corners, glass blur, gradient text or neon glow.
Don't use Unicode glyphs as icons; draw marks in CSS and hide decorative ones from assistive tech.
Don't scatter entrance animations. Keep the pinned loops slow, pause them offscreen, and preserve a reduced-motion path.
Don't let functional text drop below 11px, place brass or tinted cream on red copy, or break an Anton word with an invented bold weight.
Don't re-enable the suppressed detector rules without reading why they are pinned in .impeccable/config.json.
